traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria and technical requirements in docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md are implemented and verified by passing tests.
• Core Functionality & REQ-FUNCTION-DETECTION: Both rules enforce their annotations over the same set of function-like constructs (FunctionDeclaration, FunctionExpression, MethodDefinition, TSDeclareFunction, TSMethodSignature). Arrow functions are not in DEFAULT_SCOPE, and no scope enum value allows them, so they are excluded from enforcement by default and in configuration, matching the story’s exclusion requirement. Tests in tests/rules/require-story-annotation.test.ts and tests/rules/require-req-annotation.test.ts exercise all these node types for both valid and invalid cases.
• JSDoc Parsing & Common Strategy (REQ-JSDOC-PARSING): For @story, require-story-helpers.ts + require-story-io.ts use sourceCode.getJSDocComment, getCommentsBefore, leadingComments, and line/text heuristics. For @req, annotation-checker.ts + reqAnnotationDetection.ts apply an analogous strategy using getJSDocComment, leading comments, getCommentsBefore, and advanced heuristics (linesBeforeHasReq, parentChainHasReq, fallbackTextBeforeHasReq), reusing LOOKBACK_LINES and FALLBACK_WINDOW from require-story-io.ts. Though implemented in separate helper modules, the parsing and detection strategy is shared in structure and behavior, and tests confirm consistent treatment of @supports for both story and requirement coverage.
• Annotation Enforcement (REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED): require-story-annotation reports missing @story using a centralized coreReportMissing helper that also wires in auto-fix suggestions. require-req-annotation uses checkReqAnnotation plus missingReq message definitions and reports missing @req even when only @story is present. When both rules are enabled, in-scope functions are forced to have both a story-level marker (@story or @supports) and a requirement marker (@req or @supports), as demonstrated by tests that treat '@implements … REQ-ID' as satisfying both while still failing pure @story or pure @req where appropriate.
• Configurable Scope & Export Priority (REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE, REQ-EXPORT-PRIORITY): Both rules share DEFAULT_SCOPE and EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES and rely on the same shouldProcessNode helper. Tests explicitly cover scope filtering and exportPriority='exported'/'non-exported' behaviors for both rules, confirming consistent semantics.
• Error Location & User Experience (REQ-ERROR-LOCATION): For @story, coreReportMissing uses getNameNodeForReport to anchor errors on function identifiers or method keys, and provides message data with both name and functionName. For @req, getNameNodeForReqReport and getReportedName do the same, including a readable '(anonymous)' label for anonymous functions. Test cases assert data fields and behavior for named, anonymous, JS, and TS constructs, and both rules’ messages provide clear, imperative guidance including examples.
• TypeScript Integration (REQ-TYPESCRIPT-SUPPORT): Both rules and the shared annotation-checker support TSDeclareFunction and TSMethodSignature. This is validated by tests in tests/rules/require-story-annotation.test.ts, tests/rules/require-req-annotation.test.ts, and tests/utils/annotation-checker.test.ts using TS-enabled RuleTester configurations.
• Quality, Error Handling, and Documentation: The rules use ESLint’s recommended structure (meta, schema, messages, create) and factor complex behavior into helpers. Multiple helpers include try/catch guards so malformed JSDoc, missing loc/range, or sourceCode issues degrade gracefully instead of crashing lint runs; edge-case tests in tests/rules/require-story-helpers-edgecases.test.ts and annotation-checker tests validate this behavior. Rule documentation in docs/rules/require-story-annotation.md and docs/rules/require-req-annotation.md is aligned with the implementation, covers options and examples (JS and TS), and explicitly references this story.
Given the concrete implementation, extensive story-tagged tests, passing test suite, and aligned documentation, the story 003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS is fully implemented and passes.
